from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The Perspective Shift", [
            "Coordinates describe space like a language.",
            "Robby moves across the grid floor.",
            "Standard grid vs. tilted grid systems."
        ])

        # Animation Elements
        grid = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(grid, "C3")
        
        vector = Vector([1, 1], color="#00FFFF")
        vector.shift(grid.c2p(0, 0) - vector.get_start())
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(grid), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(GrowArrow(vector), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        label = MathTex("v", color="#00FFFF").next_to(vector.get_end(), UP)
        self.add(label)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        origin_dot = Dot(grid.c2p(0, 0), color="#FFD700")
        self.play(FadeIn(origin_dot))
        
        self.play(Rotate(grid, angle=PI/4, about_point=grid.c2p(0, 0)), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["A basis spans the vector space.", "Standard basis vectors i and j.", "Tilted alternative vectors u and v."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Basis as Building Blocks", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create vectors
        i_vec = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT, color=BLUE)
        j_vec = Arrow(ORIGIN, UP, color=BLUE)
        u_vec = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT + UP, color=YELLOW)
        v_vec = Arrow(ORIGIN, -1*RIGHT + UP, color=YELLOW)
        
        # Labels
        i_label = MathTex("i", color=BLUE)
        j_label = MathTex("j", color=BLUE)
        u_label = MathTex("u", color=YELLOW)
        v_label = MathTex("v", color=YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.place_at_grid(i_vec, 'D3')
        self.place_at_grid(j_vec, 'D3') # Initial overlap
        self.place_at_grid(i_label, 'D4')
        self.place_at_grid(j_label, 'C3')

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Build transition matrix P for conversion.",
            "Columns are new basis in standard.",
            "Matrix P maps new coordinates.",
            "Mapping basis coordinates to Cartesian space.",
            "Transition matrix links the two grids."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Change of Basis Matrix (P)", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        matrix_p = MathTex(r"P = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}", color=WHITE)
        basis_vectors = VGroup(
            MathTex(r"u = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}"),
            MathTex(r"v = \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}")
        )
        label_p = Text("P", color="#32CD32")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_p, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(matrix_p))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        self.place_at_grid(basis_vectors[0], "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(basis_vectors[1], "D4")
        self.play(FadeIn(basis_vectors))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        matrix_p.set_color("#32CD32")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        self.place_at_grid(label_p, "A2")
        self.play(Write(label_p))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Conversion Algorithm", [
            "Standard space equals P times new.",
            "Use inverse P to reverse.",
            "Visualize grid un-warping clearly.",
            "Reverse operation shows system reversibility.",
            "System conversion is fully computable."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Standard space equals P times new.
        formula1 = MathTex(r"[v]_{std} = P \cdot [v]_{new}", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(formula1, "B2")
        self.play(Write(formula1))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Use inverse P to reverse.
        formula2 = MathTex(r"[v]_{new} = P^{-1} \cdot [v]_{std}", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(formula2, "C2")
        self.play(Write(formula2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        
        p_inv = formula2[0][5:8]
        self.play(Indicate(p_inv, color="#FF69B4"))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF69B4")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Visualize grid un-warping clearly.
        visual_text = Text("Un-warping grid visual", font_size=24, color=GRAY)
        self.place_at_grid(visual_text, "D2")
        self.play(FadeIn(visual_text))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Reverse operation shows system reversibility.
        rev_text = Text("Reversibility confirmed", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(rev_text, "E2")
        self.play(Write(rev_text))
        self.lecture[3].set_color(ORANGE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # System conversion is fully computable.
        comp_text = Text("Computation Ready", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(comp_text, "F2")
        self.play(Write(comp_text))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(PURPLE)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application and Conclusion", [
            "Change of basis simplifies complex problems.",
            "Useful in graphics and physics.",
            "Shifted perspective, same underlying object."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show real-world coordinate example in #1E90FF
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#1E90FF")
        
        plane = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.5)
        vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=[1, 1, 0], color=YELLOW)
        label = MathTex(r"v", color=WHITE).next_to(vec.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)
        
        group = VGroup(plane, vec, label)
        self.place_at_grid(group, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Create(plane), GrowArrow(vec), Write(label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display updated vector position clearly
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#1E90FF")
        
        new_vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=[-0.5, 1.5, 0], color=ORANGE)
        new_label = MathTex(r"v'", color=WHITE).next_to(new_vec.get_end(), UL, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(new_vec, 'E5', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(new_label, 'D5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(new_vec), Write(new_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Final transition to summary title screen
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#1E90FF")
        
        conclusion = Text("Changing perspective,\nnot the object.", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(conclusion, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(group), FadeOut(new_vec), FadeOut(new_label), Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Perspective Shift
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a coordinate system as a 'language' to describe space. Use an animation of a robot (Robby) moving in a room. Explain that the same location in the room can be described by different grid systems (Standard Basis vs. Non-Standard Basis).
sections.example: A robot marks a point on a floor grid. If the grid lines are rotated by 45 degrees, the robot's (x, y) coordinates change, but the physical location remains identical.

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Basis as Building Blocks
sections.content: Briefly define a basis as a set of linearly independent vectors that span the space. Use graphical representation: showing vectors i=(1,0) and j=(0,1) as the default 'standard' grid, then showing two alternative vectors u and v to form a 'tilted' grid.
sections.example: Standard Basis: { (1,0), (0,1) }; Alternative Basis: { (1,1), (-1,1) }. Visualizing the vectors as arrows defines the new 'ruler' scale.

sections.title: The Change of Basis Matrix (P)
sections.content: Explain that to translate coordinates from the new basis back to the standard basis, we build a transition matrix P. Show the columns of P as the coordinates of the new basis vectors expressed in the standard basis.
sections.example: If our new basis vectors are u=(1,1) and v=(-1,1), the transition matrix P is [[1, -1], [1, 1]]. Multiplying P by a coordinate vector in the new basis maps it directly to standard Cartesian space.

sections.title: The Conversion Algorithm
sections.content: Formalize the process: [x]_std = P * [x]_new. Explain the reverse operation: to go from standard back to new, we need P-inverse. Visualize this as the 'un-warping' of the grid.
sections.example: If a bird is at [2, 1] in the 'tilted' basis, calculate its standard coordinates by P * [2, 1]^T. Then calculate the inverse to show how the system is reversible.

sections.title: Application and Conclusion
sections.content: Summarize how changing basis simplifies complex problems (e.g., Eigenvalue decomposition, computer graphics rotations). Reiterate that changing basis is simply changing our point of view, not the underlying object.
sections.example: In a 3D game engine, changing basis allows developers to calculate physics relative to an object’s local 'forward' vector rather than the static world map.
